chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Three are redeemers.' So he mentioned the third as being moderation in wealth and in poverty.
ai.seo_question: What is the third of the three redeemers mentioned by the Prophet?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Prophet (peace be upon him) outlines three paths to salvation, with the third emphasizing 'al-qasd' (moderation/balance) as the key to navigating both wealth and poverty. This concept reflects the Shia ethical ideal of avoiding the extremes of miserliness and extravagance, ensuring that one's state of being does not distract from spiritual devotion. It underscores the principle that material conditions are secondary to the balanced conduct they inspire.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Three are redeemers’. So he<sup>saww</sup> mentioned the third as being – the moderation during the prosperity as well as (during) the poverty’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mansur ibn Yunus from abu Hamzah who has said the following: “Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause,
has said, ‘Three things work as means of salvation for a person and he described moderation, in both poverty and financial well-being, to be one of such means.’”
